evidence.text: Akamai's 8-K of 2026-09-24 says it issued Jabil a build request under their existing server-manufacturing MSA and authorised Jabil to buy about $1.7bn of memory components on consignment, which Jabil buys back at cost as it uses them. The request is tied to Akamai's $11.6bn, seven-year Anthropic cloud deal, arrived after Jabil last spoke on 2026-06-17, and is for a customer and program Jabil has never quantified. With DRAM now over half of a server's bill of materials, the full build is plausibly a multi-billion-dollar FY27-28 revenue program that Jabil can fold into the FY27 guide on 2026-09-30.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line this stock trades on. The Sept 2025 FY26 guide ($31.3bn, $11.00) went -6.69% in the baseline window. The June 2026 FY raise to $35bn and $12.70, against $34.24bn and $12.38 consensus, rallied more than 10% intraday and closed -0.14% (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/jabil-beats-consensus-estimates-shares-121649461.html). March and Dec 2025 raises closed -1.4% and +1.76%. Raised guides have not been paid at the close for three prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is partly priced: JBL rose 4.8% in the afternoon session after the 8-K (https://markets.financialcontent.com/stocks/article/stockstory-2026-9-25-why-jabil-jbl-stock-is-trading-up-today). That is roughly $1.5bn of market cap, and it is also roughly what a ~$3bn program at a ~5% core margin is worth. What is not priced is the size of the program. Jabil has not said how much revenue it brings or when, and four sessions is too short for eleven analysts to rebuild FY27 models that sit at $15.60 core EPS. If the market had priced a larger program, the stock would have recovered more of the $429-to-$300 drawdown and the skew would be more call-bid than -1.1. The offset is that pass-through memory at cost adds revenue but little margin, so it can pull the FY27 margin guide below the >6% management framed in June, which the market could read as dilution.
evidence.independence: Jabil's July 2026 purchase of a 1.5m sq ft data-center-infrastructure plant in Marshall County, MS, with about 2,200 jobs (https://governorreeves.ms.gov/jabil-to-open-manufacturing-facility-in-marshall-county/, 2026-07-07), points to a capacity ramp for FY27. That is public, has no customer named, and is a separate document. Peers raised after Jabil last spoke: Flex lifted FY27 revenue to $33.7-35.2bn on 2026-07-29 and Celestica lifted 2026 to $20.5bn on 2026-07-27. That is sector evidence, not Jabil evidence.
